scenario_text: A mid-sized private bank currently runs its core banking system on a legacy COBOL framework. Management has decided to migrate the entire system to a modern Java-based framework. No new functionality is to be added — the migrated system must replicate the existing features exactly. Testing and validation is required at every stage of the migration to ensure nothing breaks. The project team consists of 2 developers and needs to be completed within 3-4 months.

requirements.statement: The system shall replicate all existing features of the legacy COBOL core banking system
requirements.business_justification: To ensure continuity of operations and avoid disruption to customers and internal processes
requirements.assumptions: The legacy system's functionality is well-documented and fully understood
requirements.acceptance_criteria: All existing features are validated and confirmed to function identically in the new system

requirements.statement: The system shall support migration of data from the legacy COBOL framework to the new Java-based framework
requirements.business_justification: To ensure seamless transition of customer and operational data without loss or corruption
requirements.assumptions: Data formats and structures are compatible between the legacy and new systems
requirements.acceptance_criteria: All data is successfully migrated and validated for accuracy and completeness

requirements.statement: The system shall support testing and validation at every stage of the migration process
requirements.business_justification: To ensure that no functionality is broken during migration and that the system remains stable
requirements.assumptions: Testing environments are available and representative of production
requirements.acceptance_criteria: All stages of migration are tested and validated with no critical issues identified
applicable_regulations: Master Direction on Information Technology Governance, Risk, Controls and Assurance Practices §14 (RBI/2023-24/107) [issued 07 Nov 2023]

requirements.statement: The system shall be implemented using a Java-based framework
requirements.business_justification: To modernize the infrastructure, improve maintainability, and reduce long-term costs
requirements.assumptions: The development team has the necessary expertise in Java and modern software development practices
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system is fully implemented using Java and runs on a supported application server

requirements.statement: The system shall be completed within 3-4 months
requirements.business_justification: To align with the organization's strategic timeline and minimize operational disruption
requirements.assumptions: The project team has sufficient resources and no major unforeseen obstacles
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system is fully migrated, tested, and ready for deployment within the specified timeframe

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a detailed migration log that tracks the status of each data element during the migration process
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The log must include timestamps, source and target data locations, and any errors encountered during migration

requirements.statement: The system shall allow administrators to configure and manage user roles and permissions during the migration process
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Administrators must be able to assign, modify, and revoke roles with granular access controls

requirements.statement: The system shall support rollback of migration steps in case of failure or validation errors
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Rollback must be initiated through a user interface and must restore the system to a previously validated state
applicable_regulations: Master Direction on Information Technology Governance, Risk, Controls and Assurance Practices §14 (RBI/2023-24/107) [issued 07 Nov 2023]

requirements.statement: The system shall provide real-time monitoring and alerting for migration progress and errors
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Alerts must be sent via email and in-app notifications for critical migration failures or delays

requirements.statement: The system shall support parallel testing of the legacy and new systems during migration
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system must allow for simultaneous execution of legacy and new system processes with isolated data sets

requirements.statement: The system shall ensure data integrity during migration by performing checksum validation on all transferred data
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Checksums must be generated and compared before and after data transfer, with discrepancies logged and reported
applicable_regulations: Master Direction on Information Technology Governance, Risk, Controls and Assurance Practices §14 (RBI/2023-24/107) [issued 07 Nov 2023]

requirements.statement: The system shall support a maximum of 10 concurrent migration tasks to ensure stability and performance
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system must enforce a limit of 10 concurrent migration processes and queue additional tasks until resources are available

dropped.statement: The system shall be developed by a team of 2 developers

issues.description: The term 'replicate all existing features' is vague and lacks a measurable definition. What constitutes an 'existing feature'? How will 'function identically' be verified?
issues.suggestion: Define 'existing features' with specific examples or reference a documented list of features from the legacy system. Specify measurable criteria for 'function identically', such as passing all existing test cases or achieving a specific level of test coverage.

issues.description: The term 'legacy COBOL core banking system' is used without a definition. While COBOL is a known programming language, the specific system is not defined.
issues.suggestion: Provide a definition or reference for the 'legacy COBOL core banking system' to ensure clarity for all stakeholders.

issues.description: The term 'support migration of data' is vague. What specific data is being migrated? What is the expected format or structure of the migrated data?
issues.suggestion: Define the scope of data migration with specific examples, such as customer records, transaction logs, or account details. Specify measurable criteria for 'accuracy and completeness', such as a percentage of data validated or a specific number of data fields checked.

issues.description: The term 'testing and validation at every stage' is vague. What specific stages are being referred to? What constitutes 'no critical issues identified'?
issues.suggestion: Define the stages of migration that require testing and validation. Specify measurable criteria for 'no critical issues identified', such as a defined severity level or a specific number of test cases passed.

issues.description: The term 'modern software development practices' is vague and lacks a measurable definition.
issues.suggestion: Define 'modern software development practices' with specific examples or reference a standard, such as Agile or DevOps.

issues.description: The term 'within 3-4 months' is vague and lacks a measurable definition. What is the exact start and end date? What constitutes 'fully migrated, tested, and ready for deployment'?
issues.suggestion: Define the exact start and end dates for the project. Specify measurable criteria for 'fully migrated, tested, and ready for deployment', such as passing all acceptance criteria or achieving a specific level of test coverage.

advantages.relevance: REQ-005 requires the system to be completed within 3-4 months, and a predictable schedule aligns with this fixed timeline.
REQ-001 and REQ-002 require replicating existing features and migrating data, which can be managed through structured phase gates ensuring each step is validated before proceeding.
REQ-001 assumes the legacy system's functionality is well-documented, and Waterfall's emphasis on documentation supports this requirement.
REQ-004 assumes the development team has the necessary expertise in Java, making it easier to manage and staff the project using a straightforward model like Waterfall.

justifications.gives_up: Waterfall assumes verification at every stage is not required — that is not the case here, so that part of its design earns nothing on this project.

sdlc.cross_check_reasoning: Spiral is the most suitable model due to its emphasis on iterative development, risk management, and thorough testing, which aligns with the high-risk, high-priority requirements for data migration and validation. Waterfall is next as it provides a structured approach for replicating legacy system features, which are well-documented and fully understood.

risk_register.title: Business continuity and disaster recovery for the system
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Master Direction on Information Technology Governance, Risk, Controls and Assurance Practices §28 (RBI/2023-24/107) [issued 07 Nov 2023])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall have a disaster recovery arrangement with defined recovery time and recovery point objectives, tested periodically under the bank's business continuity plan.

risk_register.title: Cyber incidents reported to CERT-In within 6 hours
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000 — information security practices and reporting of cyber incidents (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In) [issued 28 Apr 2022])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall support reporting cyber incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours of their being noticed, with a copy to the sector regulator.

risk_register.title: Cyber security incidents reported promptly to RBI
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Cyber Security Framework in Banks §15 (RBI/2015-16/418) [2016 framework (partly superseded by the 2023 IT directions)])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall detect and log cyber security incidents and support reporting them to RBI (and CERT-In) within the mandated timelines.

risk_register.title: ICT system logs kept for a rolling 180 days within India
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000 — information security practices and reporting of cyber incidents §6(iv) (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In) [issued 28 Apr 2022])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall keep logs of all its ICT components securely for a rolling 180 days, within India, and make them available to CERT-In on request.

risk_register.title: Transaction records kept at least five years from the date of transaction
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Master Direction — Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016 §(a) (RBI/DBR/2015-16/18) [updated 14 Aug 2025])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall retain records of all transactions with the customer for at least five years from the date of the transaction.

risk_register.title: System clocks synchronised to NIC/NPL time servers
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000 — information security practices and reporting of cyber incidents §6(i) (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In) [issued 28 Apr 2022])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall synchronise all its clocks to the NIC or NPL NTP servers (or servers traceable to them), so that log timestamps are reliable.

risk_register.title: Ambiguity in REQ-001
risk_register.cause: The term 'replicate all existing features' is vague and lacks a measurable definition. What constitutes an 'existing feature'? How will 'function identically' be verified?
risk_register.consequence: The requirement cannot be built or tested as written.
risk_register.mitigation: Define 'existing features' with specific examples or reference a documented list of features from the legacy system. Specify measurable criteria for 'function identically', such as passing all existing test cases or achieving a specific level of test coverage.

risk_register.title: Ambiguity in REQ-002
risk_register.cause: The term 'support migration of data' is vague. What specific data is being migrated? What is the expected format or structure of the migrated data?
risk_register.consequence: The requirement cannot be built or tested as written.
risk_register.mitigation: Define the scope of data migration with specific examples, such as customer records, transaction logs, or account details. Specify measurable criteria for 'accuracy and completeness', such as a percentage of data validated or a specific number of data fields checked.

risk_register.title: Ambiguity in REQ-003
risk_register.cause: The term 'testing and validation at every stage' is vague. What specific stages are being referred to? What constitutes 'no critical issues identified'?
risk_register.consequence: The requirement cannot be built or tested as written.
risk_register.mitigation: Define the stages of migration that require testing and validation. Specify measurable criteria for 'no critical issues identified', such as a defined severity level or a specific number of test cases passed.

risk_register.title: Ambiguity in REQ-005
risk_register.cause: The term 'within 3-4 months' is vague and lacks a measurable definition. What is the exact start and end date? What constitutes 'fully migrated, tested, and ready for deployment'?
risk_register.consequence: The requirement cannot be built or tested as written.
risk_register.mitigation: Define the exact start and end dates for the project. Specify measurable criteria for 'fully migrated, tested, and ready for deployment', such as passing all acceptance criteria or achieving a specific level of test coverage.

risk_register.title: Small team — key-person dependency
risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "The project team consists of 2 developers and needs to be completed within 3-4 months."
risk_register.consequence: Losing one person stalls the project.
risk_register.mitigation: Pair on critical components, document as you go, and identify a backup for each area.
evidence: The project team consists of 2 developers and needs to be completed within 3-4 months.

risk_register.title: Integrations authenticated, encrypted and rate-limited
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (practice: Industry practice (OWASP API Security Top 10)).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: Every integration with an external system shall be mutually authenticated, encrypted in transit, allow-listed and rate-limited, with failures logged.

risk_register.title: Sensitive data encrypted at rest and in transit
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (regulation: Cyber Security Framework in Banks §8.1 (RBI/2015-16/418) [2016 framework (partly superseded by the 2023 IT directions)]).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall encrypt customer and transaction data at rest and in transit using algorithms and key lengths approved under the bank's cryptographic policy.

risk_register.title: High-risk function depends on an external system (REQ-002)
risk_register.cause: REQ-002 is high risk and classified Integration: The system shall support migration of data from the legacy COBOL framework to the new Java-based framework
risk_register.consequence: An external system's availability, contract or interface change blocks a high-risk function.
risk_register.mitigation: Agree interface contracts early, stub the dependency for testing, and define fallback behaviour.

risk_register.title: High-risk function depends on an external system (REQ-003)
risk_register.cause: REQ-003 is high risk and classified Integration: The system shall support testing and validation at every stage of the migration process
risk_register.consequence: An external system's availability, contract or interface change blocks a high-risk function.
risk_register.mitigation: Agree interface contracts early, stub the dependency for testing, and define fallback behaviour.

risk_register.title: High-risk function depends on an external system (REQ-009)
risk_register.cause: REQ-009 is high risk and classified Integration: The system shall provide real-time monitoring and alerting for migration progress and errors
risk_register.consequence: An external system's availability, contract or interface change blocks a high-risk function.
risk_register.mitigation: Agree interface contracts early, stub the dependency for testing, and define fallback behaviour.

risk_register.title: Legacy migration — undocumented behaviour and data conversion
risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "A mid-sized private bank currently runs its core banking system on a legacy COBOL framework."
risk_register.consequence: Behaviour the old system relied on is lost or data is converted wrongly.
risk_register.mitigation: Inventory existing behaviour, reconcile migrated data, and run old and new in parallel before cut-over.
evidence: A mid-sized private bank currently runs its core banking system on a legacy COBOL framework.

risk_register.title: Inability to replicate legacy system behavior
risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "migrated system must replicate the existing features exactly"
risk_register.consequence: Failure to accurately replicate legacy behavior could lead to functional discrepancies, impacting customer experience and regulatory compliance.
risk_register.mitigation: Review with the project manager.
evidence: migrated system must replicate the existing features exactly

risk_register.title: Insufficient time to complete migration
risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "needs to be completed within 3-4 months"
risk_register.consequence: Project may not be completed on time, leading to delays in system migration and potential operational disruptions.
risk_register.mitigation: Review with the project manager.
evidence: needs to be completed within 3-4 months

risk_register.title: Limited testing resources due to small team
risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "project team consists of 2 developers"
risk_register.consequence: Inadequate testing may result in undetected issues during migration, increasing the risk of system failures post-deployment.
risk_register.mitigation: Review with the project manager.

risk_register.title: Security events monitored and alerted on
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (regulation: Cyber Security Framework in Banks §19.6(b) (RBI/2015-16/418) [2016 framework (partly superseded by the 2023 IT directions)]).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall forward security events to the bank's security operations monitoring and raise alerts on anomalous access or activity.

risk_register.title: Vulnerability management, patching and security testing before release
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (regulation: Cyber Security Framework in Banks §7.1 (RBI/2015-16/418) [2016 framework (partly superseded by the 2023 IT directions)]).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall undergo vulnerability assessment and penetration testing before go-live and after major changes, and its components shall be patched under the bank's patch management policy.

About “The system shall be completed within 3-4 months”: The term 'within 3-4 months' is vague and lacks a measurable definition. What is the exact start and end date? What constitutes 'fully migrated, tested, and ready for deployment'? (For example: Define the exact start and end dates for the project. Specify measurable criteria for 'fully migrated, tested, and ready for deployment', such as passing all acceptance criteria or achieving a specific level of test coverage.)

About “The system shall replicate all existing features of the legacy COBOL core banking system”: The term 'replicate all existing features' is vague and lacks a measurable definition. What constitutes an 'existing feature'? How will 'function identically' be verified? (For example: Define 'existing features' with specific examples or reference a documented list of features from the legacy system. Specify measurable criteria for 'function identically', such as passing all existing test cases or achieving a specific level of test coverage.)

About “The system shall support migration of data from the legacy COBOL framework to the new Java-based framework”: The term 'support migration of data' is vague. What specific data is being migrated? What is the expected format or structure of the migrated data? (For example: Define the scope of data migration with specific examples, such as customer records, transaction logs, or account details. Specify measurable criteria for 'accuracy and completeness', such as a percentage of data validated or a specific number of data fields checked.)

About “The system shall support testing and validation at every stage of the migration process”: The term 'testing and validation at every stage' is vague. What specific stages are being referred to? What constitutes 'no critical issues identified'? (For example: Define the stages of migration that require testing and validation. Specify measurable criteria for 'no critical issues identified', such as a defined severity level or a specific number of test cases passed.)

Integrations authenticated, encrypted and rate-limited. Should the system include: “Every integration with an external system shall be mutually authenticated, encrypted in transit, allow-listed and rate-limited, with failures logged”?

Sensitive data encrypted at rest and in transit. Should the system include: “The system shall encrypt customer and transaction data at rest and in transit using algorithms and key lengths approved under the bank's cryptographic policy”?
What business outcome is this system meant to achieve, and how will you know it has — a target processing time, volume, cost or conversion rate?

About “The system shall be implemented using a Java-based framework”: The term 'modern software development practices' is vague and lacks a measurable definition. (For example: Define 'modern software development practices' with specific examples or reference a standard, such as Agile or DevOps.)

About “The system shall provide real-time monitoring and alerting for migration progress and errors”: The term 'real-time' is vague and not measurable. It should be defined with a specific time threshold (e.g., 'within 1 second') for clarity and testability. (For example: Define 'real-time' with a measurable time threshold in the statement or acceptance criteria.)

needs_review: 5 high-severity regulatory obligation(s) have no covering requirement: Cyber incidents reported to CERT-In within 6 hours; ICT system logs kept for a rolling 180 days within India; Cyber security incidents reported promptly to RBI (and 2 more).

3 requirement(s) cite a regulation that, on reading, does not govern them: "The system shall ensure data integrity during migration by performing checksum validation on all transferred data"; "The system shall support testing and validation at every stage of the migration process" (and 1 more).
